# Linux32 output removal spans task declarations and release consumers, while saved task mappings remain data

The owned Linux x86 removal deletes the three linux/opt, linux-shippable/opt and linux/debug declarations, five Linux32 mozconfigs, platform entries and recipes for localization/repackage/deb/update verification, historical beta bouncer products, and linux32-libotr plus its i686 Linux script case. The current build loader still includes linux.yml, whose retained Linux64 tasks consume linux64-libotr and the x86_64 sysroot. Localization, repackage formats, bouncer submission and update verification each retain their own platform selectors. This is output-platform scope: Windows32 and Linux-hosted cross builds remain. Saved release fixture existing_tasks maps are historical label-to-ID data, not task declarations or proof of execution. The owned beta-promote fixture still has an unchanged build-linux/debug mapping, so a residual label alone does not prove a generated Linux32 task survives. The checked decision helper separately reads a prior full graph to produce existing-task IDs. Later enterprise/aarch64/toolchain and fixture changes stay separate from the owned removal. No graph, build, release or download-service operation was run.

Scope: taskcluster/linux32-removal.
